move.attributionBasis: In open discussion, Knechtle asks why Dillahunty uses Old Testament examples; this is Dillahunty's continuous answer applying the same objection to New Testament miracles.

responseComponents.text: A report that somebody died and returned is the supernatural claim itself, not independent empirical evidence for it.
Accurate transmission of a story would not by itself confirm the miracle narrated by that story.

move.proposition: New Testament miracle and resurrection stories remain unconfirmed supernatural claims rather than evidence establishing their own truth.
